title: Capture-phase window scroll listener also sees the floating surface's own scrollable subtree — guard composedPath or scrolling inside the menu closes it
trigger: A floating surface (select/menu/popover/tooltip) registers a capture-phase window 'scroll' listener to dismiss on outside scroll, AND the surface contains a scrollable subtree
principle: scroll does not bubble, but a capture-phase listener on window fires for scroll events targeted at ANY descendant — including the surface's own scrollable list. Scrolling/swiping inside the menu then dismisses it. Ignore events whose composedPath() includes the surface element; scrollable overlay surfaces also need overflow-y:auto (a max-height alone does not make a scroller) plus overscroll-behavior:contain so boundary gestures don't chain to the page and trigger an outside-scroll dismissal.

cases.context: Select dropdown and Menu vanished the moment the user swiped to scroll the option list — the capture listener treated the list's own scroll as an outside scroll
cases.bad: const onScroll = () => closeMenu(); win.addEventListener('scroll', onScroll, true);

cases.context: Resolve doc/window/shadow scope for the listener from a ref that is mounted before the surface exists (the trigger), not from the portaled surface — on first render the trigger ref is still null so the portal lands in document.body, and the surface element is remounted into the shadow root on the next commit; an effect that captured the surface's root at mount then listens on the wrong scope
cases.bad: const root = surfaceRef.current.getRootNode(); // surface portaled to body at effect time → scope = document, shadow scrolls missed
cases.good: const anchor = triggerRef.current ?? surfaceRef.current; const scope = anchor.getRootNode(); // trigger is a normal element, always in the right tree

applyFor: any close-on-scroll dismissal for fixed/portal surfaces
Select, Menu, Popover, SpeedPill, ProfileMenu, HintIcon-style popovers
scrollable overlays inside shadow DOM (scroll is non-composed — needs a scope-level listener)
